items.kind: performance / tooling (the reuse gate reads the entry's text; S)
items.title: The macro-defining bypass of the base cache is textual: an entry whose TEXT contains `macro` (`entry_source.contains("macro")` in `analyze_inner`'s `base_cacheable`) - a comment or a string that says the word - is uncacheable, so it gets no base-cache hit and never takes the std prefix; 4 of the 147 corpus programs (`crypto`, `db`, `file`, `watch`) say it only in a comment
items.body: The gate stands in for 'this entry DEFINES a macro', whose definitions would register into the registry the stored world carries (E23's entanglement). N179 now names it in the census (`prefix-refusal macro-text`). Rec: decide it from the parsed tree (a top-level `macro fun` definition, or whatever `macros::register_file` would register) rather than the text; the four corpus programs then take the prefix. Not built in incr-55 (it moves which programs are cached, so it wants its own estate count).

items.title: An impl-reach verdict asked AFTER `build()` reads a package blanket binder differently from the same verdict asked before it: the tier oracle's log (std's questions, asked under std's rigid binder scopes) against `impl type T { fun len(self): i32 }` in a package module hits `member len` before `build()` and does not after
items.body: Found building P6a's oracle (which therefore asks where section 4.2's guard asked, as the entry is about to walk). `impl_subject_admits(receiver, Generic(binder))` under a rigid `rigid_binder_scope` answers differently once `build()` has run. M121's own post-build verdict (`impl_reach`, the entry's and a hot set's impls) still hits an ENTRY blanket asked about a package's rigid `List<T>` (0.52.0: `impl-reached member len (hot false, entry true)`), so it is narrower than every blanket; whether an S1 hot blanket against a std question the package half re-asks can be missed there is the open question. Rec: find what `build()` changes about the binder's admission and ask the verdict before `build()` or under the pre-build state; pin with the oracle fixture.

items.title: On the owner's CURRENT kolt (a `cp -r` of the working tree past b04095a, lucide carried) E292's rows read 3-7x the Order 54 seal's under v0.52.0 itself - leaf keystroke 2,360 ms CPU / 8.41 G instructions to idle (the seal on kolt@611d86f7: 330 ms / 2.53 G), css keystroke 2,270 ms / 8.06 G - and four scenarios cannot be measured at all: the `model.vl` keystroke rows' and the `parse break`/`repair` rows' anchors are gone from the source (N174 again)
items.body: lsp-latency.py --runs 5 at load 12-15 (CPU columns load-polluted; instructions are the comparison). The served leaf analysis is seeded (post-seam seeded+record+matches+cold, records-served 41-44, instances-served 33, hover-rows-restored 24,458) yet its checks phase is ~1.0-1.7 s: the top passes on the leaf keystroke (VILAN_PHASE_TIMING=passes, CPU ms at load ~14) are `check_view_escape` 180-530, contexts+graph 200 (post-pass), `LastUse::compute` 45-125, `check_generic_bound_satisfaction` 45-90, `infer_bumps` 45-100, `plan_resource_drops` 30-110 (M156/M163's premise was ~4 ms), the hover rows 55-75. The E292 series needs re-anchoring on this kolt (new anchors for the model.vl and parse-break rows) and a new baseline before Order 56's incr item picks its door; `check_view_escape` first (it is not served from a record on a keystroke).
